newsitem.title: USA: Drug companies post higher profits, sales.
newsitem.headline: Drug companies post higher profits, sales.

text.p: Merck & Co. Inc. and Schering-Plough Corp., two major pharmaceutical companies, both said Wednesday that stronger sales in the third quarter pushed their profits higher.
Johnson & Johnson, which manufactures prescription drugs as well as a wide variety of consumer products, also posted higher profits.

Merck said strong domestic and international sales in the three months ended Sept. 30 pushed its net income up 16 percent to $1.0 billion, or 83 cents a share, from $861.9 million, or 70 cents a share.

The company, based in Whitehouse Station, N.J., said its sales grew by 19 percent to $4.98 billion from $4.17 billion, although a strong dollar compared with most major currencies reduced sales growth by 2 percentage points.
Schering-Plough said strong sales of its prescription drugs in the period helped drive its net income up 15 percent to $291.7 million, or 79 cents a share, from $252.6 million, or 68 cents a share.

The company, based in Madison, N.J., said sales increased 10 percent to $1.4 billion from $1.3 billion, although the stronger dollar had a negative effect of about 2 percentage points on sales growth.
Johnson & Johnson, based in New Brunswick, N.J., said its third-quarter net income rose to $750 million, or 56 cents a share, from $623 million, or 48 cents a share.
The company, which sells products in 175 countries, said revenues climbed 20 percent to $5.4 billion from $4.7 billion, although the stronger dollar decreased sales by 1.8 percent.

Merck said its results were paced by sales gains for Zocor and Mevacor, two cholesterol-lowering drugs; Vasotec for treatment of high blood pressure; Proscar to treat enlarged prostate glands, and Pepcid for the treatment of ulcers.

Also contributing to sales gains were several drugs introduced last year, including Cozaar, a new class of anti-hypertensive drug, Fosamax, a nonhormonal medicine for the treatment of osteoporosis, and anti-glaucoma medicine Trusopt.
The company also said its Merck-Medco Managed Care unit, which manages pharmacy benefits for employers and insurers, continued to expand.

For the first nine months Merck said its net income climbed by 15 percent to $2.8 billion, or $2.33 a share, from $2.5 billion, or $2 a share. Nine-month sales gained 19 percent to $14.4 billion from $12.1 billion.

Schering-Plough said its sales of pharmaceutical products grew by 13 percent to $1.24 billion from $1.10 billion but health care products sales slipped 10 percent to $137.5 million from $152.8 million.
The company said the decrease in health care products revenues was largely due to lower sales of over-the-counter products, especially sun care items.

Schering said its higher worldwide sales were led by its Claritin line of nonsedating allergy medications, the world's No. 1 antihistamine brand, which were up 73 percent, and by Intron A, an antiviral and anticancer agent, up 21 percent
The company said net income for the first nine months grew 45 percent to $935.4 million, or $2.54 a share, from $647.2 million, or $1.74 a share.
Sales for the period grew 11 percent to $4.2 billion from $3.8 billion, with sales of pharmaceutical products increasing and health care products declining.
Schering-Plough's stock lost 75 cents to $64.25 in afternoon trading, Merck gained 75 cents to $72 and Johnson and Johnson lost 12.5 cents to $51.125 -- all on the New York Stock Exchange.
